title: Repo-local lore skill: drop skill_source = plugin while the plugin is off in this checkout
description:
Opum-doc ruling DEC-238 (a1), 2026-10-25T06:47:40Z (record: opum-doc PR chore/dec-238-a1), verbatim: "while opum-lore is off in a checkout, workers get the lore skill from a REPO-LOCAL generated SKILL.md. The 2026-10-20 per-checkout setting is left untouched, whatever its reason. A repository returns to skill_source = "plugin" only once the plugin is measured enabled in its own checkout. Each plugin-source repository with the plugin off in its checkout drops the skill_source = "plugin" line, runs `lore agents`, and confirms --check exits 0, as its own tier-2 decision, scheduled in the plan."

Amended by DEC-238 (a2), opum-doc, 2026-10-25T06:54:02Z (record: opum-doc PR chore/dec-238-a2), and then by DEC-238 (a3)/(a4), opum-doc, 2026-10-25T07:18:35Z (records: opum-ai/opum-doc#1354 and #1355). (a3) replaces the unsatisfiable clause: the "plugin-claude disabled" line reports the untouched 2026-10-20 override and is expected to remain, while "absent-plugin-sourced" must disappear. The full rulings, the before-state at the pinned version, and the sequencing rule are in the notes.

Measured on origin/dev 86c03ab, 2026-10-25, at the CI-pinned lore 0.13.0: .lore/config.toml sets skill_source = "plugin"; the gitignored .claude/settings.local.json sets "opum-lore@opum": false; lore agents --check prints "absent-plugin-sourced .claude/skills/lore/SKILL.md" and "plugin-claude disabled opum-lore@opum scope=user", exit 0; claude plugin list shows opum-lore@opum 0.14.1, scope user, disabled. So at runtime this checkout has no lore skill.

The change: drop the skill_source = "plugin" line from .lore/config.toml, run lore agents so the repo-local .claude/skills/lore/SKILL.md is generated and committed, and confirm lore agents --check no longer reports absent-plugin-sourced and that both checks exit 0.

This edits this repository's own governing files, so it is this repository's tier-2 decision, not an instruction from the relay; it is scheduled in the day's plan and startable only then. SEQUENCING per (a3): GCLI-22, the quest/lore 0.14.1 move, lands first when the plan allows; if it has not landed, this task measures lore check at the CI-pinned version (npx @opum-ai/lore@0.13.0 check) and says so. Scope guard from the relay: leave .claude/settings.local.json and the plugin's disabled state alone.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The .lore/config.toml no longer sets skill_source = "plugin", and the generated repo-local .claude/skills/lore/SKILL.md exists and is committed in the same change.

After the change, lore agents --check no longer reports "absent-plugin-sourced" (where it did before) and reports the Claude skill file up-to-date; the "plugin-claude disabled opum-lore@opum scope=user" line is expected to remain while the 2026-10-20 per-checkout override stands and is not a failure.

lore agents --check and lore check both exit 0, with lore check measured at this repository CI-pinned lore version as CI runs it (npx @opum-ai/lore@0.13.0 check) rather than a newer local binary; GCLI-22 lands first when the plan allows, and if it has landed the measurement follows the new pin.

The regenerated lore:agents block in CLAUDE.md no longer tells readers the skill comes only from the plugin; this repository has no hand-written drift sentence to amend, so the block is regenerated rather than hand-edited, and if lore agents still writes the plugin wording after skill_source stops being "plugin" that is a lore-cli template defect to file.
No change is made to .claude/settings.local.json or to the plugin enabled state, and skill_source = "plugin" returns only when a later measurement shows opum-lore enabled in this checkout.

implementationNotes: DEC-238 (a2), opum-doc ruling 2026-10-25T06:54:02Z (record: opum-doc PR chore/dec-238-a2), verbatim: "(1) CORRECTED: "--check exits 0" proves nothing, because it already passes broken. The criterion is: after the change, lore agents --check no longer reports "absent-plugin-sourced" or "plugin-claude disabled"; .claude/skills/lore/SKILL.md exists; and lore agents --check and lore check both exit 0. Record the before-state on the task so it is proved both ways. (2) YES, explicitly: where hand-written CLAUDE.md says a .claude/skills/ copy is drift (opum-agent line 531, quest-web, ward-cli, and any other phrasing), the owner amends that sentence in the SAME change. It now says the repo-local skill is expected while opum-lore is off in the checkout, under DEC-238 (a1). That is the owner's tier-2 decision; I name the sentence and instruct no edit. (3) opum-quest is intended, and nothing changes. It is off at user scope by the operator's first-party answer of 2026-10-12 (DEC-172 (4bf)). Quest guidance reaches workers through each CLAUDE.md's managed quest block, which points at `quest instructions`. No repo-local quest skill is restored (ODOC-142 retired it), and re-enabling is the operator's call."

BEFORE-STATE, measured in this checkout on origin/dev c367ae0, 2026-10-25, under host lore 0.14.1 (lore --version). `lore agents --check` printed: absent-plugin-sourced .claude/skills/lore/SKILL.md; up-to-date CLAUDE.md; plugin-claude disabled opum-lore@opum scope=user; plugin-claude-remedy claude plugin enable opum-lore@opum --scope user. It exited 0, so the exit code alone certifies nothing, exactly as (a2)(1) says. `lore check` in the same run exited 6 with 11 schema-drift errors (.lore/schemas/*.schema.json no longer match what 0.14.1 generates); that is the GCLI-22 pin drift, not the skill question, and the Docs job under the CI-pinned lore 0.13.0 is green at this SHA. Record the after-state under the same lore version, with the full report lines and both exit codes, so the change is proved both ways.

ON (a2)(2): this repository has NO hand-written CLAUDE.md sentence calling a .claude/skills/ copy drift. The equivalent claim — "**Skill:** installed from the `opum-lore` Claude Code plugin, not this repository — how to drive lore." — is CLAUDE.md line 17, inside the generated lore:agents managed block (between the lore:agents:begin and lore:agents:end markers). It moves with `lore agents` regenerating after skill_source is dropped; a hand edit there would be overwritten on the next regeneration. So there is no sentence that needs a hand amendment in the same change; instead the change checks that the regenerated block no longer tells readers the skill comes only from the plugin. No other CLAUDE.md line names the skill.

DEC-238 (a3) and (a4), opum-doc, 2026-10-25T07:18:35Z, verbatim (records: (a3) opum-ai/opum-doc#1354, merged; (a4) opum-ai/opum-doc#1355, lands on dev when green).

POINT 1, DEC-238 (a3), on opum-desktop's measurement (OFUS-96, opum-ai/opum-desktop#159). QCLI-530 is the fifth owner and amends the same way. (a2)(1) was unsatisfiable. The "plugin-claude disabled ... scope=user" line reports the 2026-10-20 override itself, which (a1) leaves untouched, so it stays after a correct fix. RULED A: The criterion is now: after the change, lore agents --check no longer reports "absent-plugin-sourced" (where it did before) and reports the Claude skill file up-to-date; .claude/skills/lore/SKILL.md exists; lore agents --check and lore check both exit 0. The "plugin-claude disabled" line is EXPECTED to remain while the override stands, and is not a failure. Record the before-state on the task. Owners who encoded (a2)(1)'s literal clause (QWEB-105, WCLI-79, GCLI-23, LWEB-132, QCLI-530, and any other) amend it to this wording. SEQUENCING: measure lore check at the repository's CI-pinned lore version, as CI runs it (e.g. npx @opum-ai/lore@pinned check), not with a newer local binary. Where a version-drift task (LWEB-130, GCLI-22, ...) is open in the same repository, it lands first when the plan allows; otherwise the (a1) task measures at the pinned version and says so.

POINTS 2 AND 3, DEC-238 (a4). Point 2, our reading is right: (a2)(2) covers HAND-WRITTEN prose only. A sentence inside a managed block (lore:agents, or the Quest block) is corrected by regenerating that block, never by hand. If lore agents still writes the "plugin" wording after skill_source stops being "plugin", that is a lore-cli template defect to file. quest-cli and glyph-cli have nothing to do under (a2)(2). Point 3, QCLI-531, RULED A: the exit code is unchanged, and the output states that state: current covers the managed block only, not plugin enablement.

BEFORE-STATE AT THE PINNED VERSION (supersedes the version mix in the earlier before-state note). Measured in this checkout on origin/dev 86c03ab, 2026-10-25, with npm exec --yes --package @opum-ai/lore@0.13.0 -- lore ..., the version the Docs job resolves. lore --version printed 0.13.0. lore agents --check printed: absent-plugin-sourced .claude/skills/lore/SKILL.md; up-to-date CLAUDE.md; plugin-claude disabled opum-lore@opum scope=user; plugin-claude-remedy claude plugin enable opum-lore@opum --scope user. Exit 0, so the exit code alone certifies nothing. lore check printed: Agent profiles: 4 read, 0 over capacity; 6 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 out-of-bundle links skipped. Exit 0. The host-binary run of lore check at 0.14.1 exited 6 with 11 schema-drift errors; that is the pin drift GCLI-22 owns, and it disappears when checked at 0.13.0, which is why (a3) says to measure at the pinned version. Under (a3) the "plugin-claude disabled ... scope=user" line is expected to remain after a correct fix, because it reports the 2026-10-20 per-checkout override that (a1) leaves untouched; the line that must disappear is "absent-plugin-sourced".
